text: Billions in insurance and banking still run on COBOL. Rewriting it is easy. Proving the rewrite behaves exactly the same is the hard part. This is COBOL Phoenix.

We import an insurance rating system. It is parsed deterministically, with no AI guessing: three programs, three copybooks, twenty seven business rules, and four constructs we do not support, each reported with its exact line.
Every dependency points to real source. Here is the base premium rule: its inputs, its outputs, and the compute rounded statement, cited to the original lines.
One click generates a FastAPI service, with decimal arithmetic and schemas derived from the COBOL picture clauses. Every Python statement maps back to the COBOL line it came from.

Now the proof. The original program runs in a sandboxed GnuCOBOL container with no network, and the generated Python runs beside it. Fixtures, boundary values derived from the code, edge cases and random records. One hundred twenty seven of one hundred twenty seven cases are identical, and mutation analysis shows the tests catch every fault that changes behaviour.
Does the verifier actually catch mistakes? We inject one tiny fault: a missing rounded. Eight cases fail, down to the cent, with the exact field and its copybook line.

And it is not just our sample. On an independent public insurance repository, the generated underwriting service matches GnuCOBOL on one hundred eighty of one hundred eighty cases. Mutation analysis even exposed a business rule that can never fire.
Evidence for every rule. Proof for every build. COBOL Phoenix. Preserve the logic, rebuild the future.
